outcome: Duration of labor (first stage, second stage, total)
cohort: 744 Robson class 1 women who delivered at the University Hospital of Modena between January 1, 2019, and December 31, 2019
finding: Epidural analgesia was not associated with an increased risk of cesarean or operative vaginal delivery in Robson class 1 women, although it was linked to longer labor duration, particularly the first stage.
mod_finding: The study found that epidural analgesia use during labor was not associated with an increased risk of cesarean delivery or operative vaginal delivery in Robson class 1 women.
